To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a deep neural network can be trained to recognize faces in the wild, (ii) the network can be trained using the largest facial dataset, (iii) the network learns to align faces using 3D modeling, (iv) the learned representations can be generalized to unseen faces in the wild.
(i) a large-scale dataset of facial images is essential for training deep neural network architectures for face recognition, and (ii) a model-based alignment is crucial to obtain a good performance.

(a) the alignment step in face verification is crucial, and can be performed accurately using explicit 3D modeling; and (b) a nine-layer deep network trained on a large dataset of four million images can learn to represent faces in an extremely discriminative way, and achieve human-level performance on face verification.
